## Can I Salary Sacrifice My Mortgage? A Guide to Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

If you're asking 'can i salary sacrifice my mortgage', the first step is understanding your gross annual income. This guide explains how to convert your hourly rate to a yearly figure, including the assumptions about hours, tax, super, and the differences between minimum wages, award rates, and casual loading.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard formula used by [the timesheet](/) is:

**Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. So if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is an estimate, not a determination of your pay.

### Understanding Your Fortnightly Pay

Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. Using the example above, weekly pay is $30 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280. Many employers pay fortnightly, so this figure helps you budget.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates vs Casual Loading

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage (NMW). From 1 July 2026, the NMW is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most employees are covered by an award or registered agreement that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. For example, a retail award might require $28 per hour for a Level 1 employee.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For the NMW, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using [the timesheet](/), you can check a box to add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Under the Superannuation Guarantee, your employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund. This is paid on top of your hourly rate, not deducted from it. For example, if your base rate is $30 per hour, your employer pays an extra $3.60 per hour into super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice can affect your super.

### Tax and Medicare in 2026–27

The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale for residents. For 2026–27:
- Nil tax on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Most taxpayers also pay a 2% Medicare levy. The Medicare levy surcharge (for singles without private hospital cover) and HELP repayments are not included in this estimate. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides more detail on after-tax calculations.

### State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) for full-time adult ordinary-time employees. The May 2026 national average was $2,083.70 per week. However, this figure masks significant differences between states and territories. For example, Western Australia often has higher average earnings due to the mining industry, while Tasmania tends to be lower. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page breaks down these state averages.

When using the hourly-to-annual conversion, remember that your actual earnings may differ from national averages. Your award, enterprise agreement, or individual contract sets your rate. The [pay guides](/blog) page links to Fair Work Ombudsman resources for specific industries.

### Salary Sacrifice and Your Mortgage

Now to the key question: 'can i salary sacrifice my mortgage'? Salary sacrifice (or salary packaging) is an arrangement where you forgo part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for a benefit, such as mortgage payments. This reduces your taxable income, potentially lowering your tax. However, not all employers offer this, and there are limits set by the ATO. For example, some public sector and not-for-profit employers allow salary packaging for mortgage payments, but private sector employees may have fewer options.

To assess if salary sacrifice is worthwhile, you need your gross annual income first. Use [the timesheet](/) to convert your hourly rate to annual, then discuss with your employer or a tax professional. Remember that salary sacrifice can affect your super guarantee (since it's based on ordinary earnings) and your tax offsets.

### Important Assumptions and Limitations

This guide provides an estimate only. The annual pay calculation assumes:
- A consistent 38-hour week every week
- No unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances
- No salary sacrifice deductions
- Super at 12% of ordinary earnings, capped at $270,830
- Tax using the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold
- Medicare levy at 2% using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds (the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this reference)

HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. For a personalised assessment, consult the [reference tables](/data) or speak to a qualified accountant.

### Summary

Whether you're negotiating a salary or asking 'can i salary sacrifice my mortgage', understanding your hourly-to-annual conversion is essential. Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 for a quick estimate, then adjust for your actual hours, award rate, and casual loading. Remember that super is paid on top, tax is progressive, and state averages vary. The [about the timesheet](/about) page explains how the calculator works.
